card.title: Nintendo Switch USB Charger Fuse and BQ24193 Charging Diagnostics

claims.statement: The USB charger fuse protects power from the USB-C port to the battery chip and can be replaced with a Matsuo R-rated equivalent such as the Littelfuse 0438035WRA.
claims.evidence: Checking continuity across the fuse with a multimeter in continuity mode.
claims.quote: Lets check the fuse that lets power from USB C reach the battery chip. Unplug the battery. With a multimeter set to continuity mode, put one probe in one side of the fuse and the other probe in the other side of the fuse

claims.statement: If the battery voltage increases after 30 minutes of charging, the BQ24193 charging IC is functioning.
claims.evidence: Measuring battery cable voltages before and after 30 minutes on charge.
claims.quote: After the 30 minutes, unplug it of the charger, redo everything that I said. If the voltage after 30 minutes is higher than it was, you can assume that your console is charging so the BQ24193 is fine.

claims.statement: When a charger is plugged in, BQ24193 Pin 1 should read 5V-15V, Pin 2 should be low, Pin 3 should be 0V, and Pin 4 should be low during charge or high when complete.
claims.evidence: Voltage checks on BQ24193 pins during charging.
claims.quote: Pin 1 VBus should be high 5v-15v depending on charger pin 2 if using the nintendo charger this pin should read low pin 3 Should be low 0v pin 4 should be low if charge in progress, if this pin is high charge is complete

claims.statement: Thermal set resistor values (such as 3.8k and 5.6k) connected to the BQ24193 are critical for setting charging parameters relative to battery temperature.
claims.evidence: Deviating from specific resistance values causes charging to be disabled out of range.
claims.quote: So the 3.8 k and 5.6 k values are critical and its used to set the charghing related to temperature of the battery. (bq 24193 tipical aplication recommend 2.2 k and 6.86k for ts1 and ts2 pins)

procedure: Unplug the battery and set the multimeter to continuity mode to check the USB charger fuse.
Unplug the battery and measure initial DC voltages on the exposed copper of the battery connector red cables using the black probe on a black cable.
Plug the battery back in, connect the charger for 30 minutes without pressing the power button, unplug, and re-measure the red cable voltages to confirm the battery is accepting a charge.
Check voltages on BQ24193 pins 1 through 4 with a charger plugged in.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Matsuo R-rated fuses have a 0.315A rating which is far too low; ensure proper replacement ratings.
card.caveats: Always measure in-circuit values as a comparative baseline only.
